topStories.headline: SFMTA Rolls Out Expanded Pay-or-Permit Parking in Hayes Valley
topStories.dek: After board approval in June, the city's expanded parking program is now in its implementation phase across additional blocks of Hayes Valley.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency is in the midst of an eight-month implementation process for its expanded Pay-or-Permit Parking program in Hayes Valley, following approval by the SFMTA Board of Directors on June 2, 2026. The program extends metered parking requirements to additional residential and mixed-use blocks surrounding Octavia and Hayes streets, building on a pilot program that has been in place in parts of the neighborhood since 2023.

Under the Pay-or-Permit system, residents with valid neighborhood permits can park for free on designated blockfaces, while visitors are required to pay at meters rather than following two-hour time limits. The SFMTA says the approach is designed to increase parking availability, reduce the time drivers spend circling for spots, and improve turnover that benefits local businesses.

Community reception has been mixed. During a multi-month outreach period from late 2025 through spring 2026, residents cited frustration with limited parking availability as a top concern and expressed strong interest in a Resident Guest Discount Pilot program. Some business owners and advocacy groups have raised concerns about compliance and enforcement transparency, noting that an earlier evaluation of the Hayes Valley pilot showed visitor compliance rates of around 34 percent.

SFMTA officials say the implementation — including installation of new meters and updated signage — is expected to take approximately eight months from the June 2026 board vote. Residents and businesses with questions can contact the agency at ParkingProjects@SFMTA.com.

topStories.headline: Divisadero Corridor Still Rebuilding After Back-to-Back Restaurant Fires
topStories.dek: Che Fico and The Mill — two beloved NoPa institutions on adjacent blocks of Divisadero — remain closed months after separate fires, leaving a hole in the neighborhood's dining scene.
topStories.body:
Two of the NoPa corridor's most celebrated food businesses remain shuttered this summer following separate fires that struck within three weeks of each other in June. Che Fico, the acclaimed California-Italian taverna at 838 Divisadero, has been closed since June 11 after a chimney flue fire at neighboring Foghorn Taproom caused significant damage. Co-owner David Nayfeld pledged the restaurant would rebuild and reopen, and Mayor Daniel Lurie and Supervisor Bilal Mahmood have both been in contact with the Che Fico team.

Less than three weeks later, a second fire tore through the back of The Mill at 736 Divisadero in the early hours of June 29, closing the beloved café and Josey Baker Bread bakery indefinitely. No injuries were reported in either fire. The SFFD confirmed the cause of The Mill fire was accidental and successfully contained it before it could spread to adjacent buildings.

A GoFundMe campaign for The Mill raised nearly $95,000 to help cover repairs and staff costs. Josey Baker has since moved the bread-making operation temporarily to another facility, and Josey Baker Bread loaves have returned to shelves at Bi-Rite and other neighborhood grocers — a sign that some functions are recovering even as the café itself undergoes major repairs.

Both closures have left a tangible gap in a corridor that had become one of the city's most vibrant food destinations. Neighborhood observers note that other Divisadero mainstays, including Nopa restaurant, Bar Crudo, and 4505 Burgers & BBQ, remain fully operational.

topStories.headline: SFJAZZ Center Kicks Off Bold 2026-27 Season Under New Artistic Director Terence Blanchard
topStories.dek: The Franklin Street anchor launches a new season titled 'Forward Motion,' featuring Branford Marsalis, Christian McBride, Hiromi, and centennial celebrations of Miles Davis and John Coltrane.
topStories.body:
The SFJAZZ Center at 201 Franklin Street is opening its 2026-27 season — branded 'Forward Motion' — under Executive Artistic Director Terence Blanchard and CEO Gabrielle Armand. The season spans nine months and more than 300 shows, with programming designed to connect jazz's legacy to contemporary innovation.

Highlights in the coming weeks include bassist Christian McBride at Miner Auditorium on September 10 and 11, and saxophonist Branford Marsalis on September 18 and 19. The season also features centennial celebrations of Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Antonio Carlos Jobim, and Ray Brown, alongside performances by rising artists including Isaiah Collier, Tyreek McDole, and Gabrielle Cavassa.

The SFJAZZ Center, which opened in 2013 as the only stand-alone facility built specifically for jazz in the United States, sits at the heart of Hayes Valley's performing arts corridor — steps from Davies Symphony Hall and the War Memorial Opera House. The organization serves more than 200,000 fans and students annually through its concert, commissioning, and education programs.

Tickets and a full season calendar are available at sfjazz.org. SFJAZZ is also offering new flexible ticket packages for the 2026-27 season.

moreNews.headline: Alamo Square Apartment Fire Displaces 19 Residents
moreNews.body: A fire broke out early August 6 in a three-story residential building on the 800 block of Fillmore Street near Grove Street in the Alamo Square neighborhood. San Francisco firefighters rescued 18 people from the second and third floors using ground and aerial ladders. One person was injured and 19 residents from four units were displaced. The American Red Cross was dispatched to assist those affected. The fire spread to the third floor but was contained and declared under control by approximately 3:35 a.m. SFFD Chief Dean Crispen commended crew performance in a social media post following the incident.

moreNews.headline: Hayes Valley Farmers Market Completes First Summer as a Neighborhood Fixture
moreNews.body: The Hayes Valley Farmers' Market, launched on June 6, 2026 in partnership with the Pacific Coast Farmers' Market Association, the Hayes Valley Merchants Council, and the Hayes Valley Neighborhood Association, has settled into its weekly Saturday routine on the 400-450 block of Hayes Street. The market operates from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. every Saturday through December 26 and is considered a milestone for a neighborhood that has worked for years to strengthen its commercial corridor and community identity. The market will skip only two Saturdays per year — the July 4th weekend and the day of the Hayes Valley Carnival.

moreNews.headline: SFJAZZ Launches 'Forward Motion' Season with New Leadership
moreNews.body: SFJAZZ has unveiled its 2026-27 season, titled 'Forward Motion,' under Executive Artistic Director Terence Blanchard and CEO Gabrielle Armand. The season runs nine months and features more than 300 shows at the SFJAZZ Center on Franklin Street in Hayes Valley, as well as venues citywide. The programming includes centennial tributes to Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Antonio Carlos Jobim, and Ray Brown, plus performances by icons including Dianne Reeves, Ron Carter, and Hiromi. The season opens with Christian McBride on September 10-11 at Miner Auditorium.
